newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy confirms ex-SS gets Italian, German pensions.
newsitem.headline: Italy confirms ex-SS gets Italian, German pensions.

text.p: A German ex-SS major, due to stand trial next month for his part in Italy's worst World War Two atrocity, draws state pensions from Italy and Germany, the Italian national pensions body INPS said on Saturday.
INPS said in a statement that Karl Hass, 84, receives a 199,200 lire ($117) monthly payment from Italy as well as about 900,000 lire ($530) a month from Germany.

It said the Italian payment related to "10 years of contributions paid in for work carried out in Italy in the 1950s and 1960s" and said it was legitimate since there was no law in Italy against paying pensions to people accused of war crimes.

Hass and former SS captain Erich Priebke are accused of complicity in multiple murder for their roles in the massacre of 335 men and boys at the Ardeatine Caves near Rome on March 24, 1944. Seventy-five of the victims were Jews.

Hass is expected to stand trial on April 14 and judicial sources said Priebke's re-trial could take place at the same time. Priebke was found guilty at a trial last August but freed because of circumstances triggering a statute of limitations.
He was re-arrested that night after relatives of the massacre's victims and other protesters laid seige to the courthouse. The August verdict was quashed on appeal in October.
Hass' lawyer told a military court hearing on Friday that set the trial date that his client received the pension for "services in the interest of the Italian state".

Lawyer Stefano Maccioni displayed pension documents and said the payment related to the search and recovery of bodies of German soldiers in Italy and was not related to work Hass did for the Italian secret services after the war.
Labour Minister Tiziano Treu reacted to the news by presenting a draft bill that would revoke pensions paid to anyone found guilty of war crimes against Italians.
Hass has been under house arrest at a private clinic near Rome since last June when he fractured his pelvis trying to flee from a hotel to avoid testifying at Priebke's trial.
Priebke, who is being held at a military prison in Rome, admits shooting two victims but said he had to follow orders or be killed. Hass has also admitted a role in the massacre. ($1=1,700 lire)
